messages:
sara: Pager: saw a sharp latency cliff on cb-serving in us-west-2, KV cache memory spiked and batching collapsed around 17:12 UTC. Root ts 1769994321. tagging oncall.
oncall-bot: SEV2 alert for service cb-serving: continuous-batching latency > 500ms for 2+ minutes, rate-limited fallback triggered. Pager routed to eng-oncall.
kevin: I can grab this, stepping in. any customer impact yet?
maya: yes, upstream dashboards show 504s for two large tenants (AcmePay, DataMeridian) and some token cost blowup. Requests queuing at the front end and microbatch sizes jump from ~8 to >200 intermittently.
alex: hypothesis: KV cache regen cascade + microburst alignment causing big batches that overflow disk-backed KV windows -> eviction storm. We've seen similar but not with this magnitude.
sara: logs: ```
[17:11:58] kv_cache: entries=1.2M evict_rate=3400/s miss_rate=28%
[17:12:12] batcher: in_flight=4200 queued=1600 avg_microbatch=178
[17:12:23] perf: tail_latency_p90=790ms p99=1.8s
```
chris: rolling metrics show continuous-batching threshold logic hit a path where jitter synchronized across workers: many requests align and form mega-batches.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-1769994321. Handoff to oncall engineers.
kevin: immediate mitigation plan: 1) enable cb-degen-mode to force deterministic small microbatches, 2) throttle prefetchers for 30s, 3) patch batch_max to 256, 4) temporarily increase fallback rate. I'll run 1 & 2 now.
alex: I'll prepare the patch for batch_max and a conservative jitter spread change. pushing a hotpatch to staging first.
sara: please post the exact commands / config so SREs can apply in other regions. we need cross-region parity.
kevin: running commands:
```
# enable degen mode
kubectl -n production set env deploy/cb-batcher CB_DEGEN_MODE=true
# reduce prefetch concurrency
kubectl -n production set env deploy/cb-prefetch PREFETCH_LIMIT=8
```
ops-bot: env changes applied to deployment/cb-batcher in us-west-2 (rollout started).
maya: after degen-mode and prefetch limit: queued dropped from 1600 -> 300 within 45s, p90 latency fell to ~220ms. initial 504s for AcmePay down to near-zero.
alex: hotpatch ready. patch diff (short): ```
- batch_max = 512
+ batch_max = 256
- jitter_spread_ms = 5
+ jitter_spread_ms = 40
```
I'll deploy to canary (2 pods) then observe for 5 minutes.
deploy-bot: rollout started: cb-batcher v3.14-hotfix -> canary(2/20). Healthchecks running.
chris: telemetry: cache miss-rate dropping, eviction_rate down by ~70% in canary traffic. good sign.
sara: handoff: I'm handing to alex for the hotpatch rollout and postmortem notes. I'm staying until AcmePay svc stable.
oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: sara -> alex.
alex: canary looks stable for 6m, ramping to 40% now. will push to 100% in 10m if no regressions.
maya: customer comms: notifying AcmePay ops that we had transient 504s affecting a subset of high-concurrency flows; we mitigated and are rolling a hotfix. draft sent, waiting approval.
kevin: one oddity: cache regeneration originated from a long-tail tenant job that spuriously issued many small prefills at once. we'll add guardrails to prefill path in follow-up.
sara: add to postmortem: prefill guard, safer default batch_max, increased jitter, and rate-limits on prefill. also include playbook steps we used.
chris: note for postmortem metrics: include microbatch size distribution, KV eviction rate, and time-to-recover per region.
alex: rolling to 100% now.```

Note: this thread contains root message + replies in chronological order. All times UTC.
